Personas and missions (role-play, "larp")

A persona is who the bot pretends to be. At fidelity 0 it plays the core rules to win; near 1 it copies its period, flaws and all. Traits tagged larp lore (role-play flavour) are not from the sources and switch on only at fidelity 0.7 or more. Retreat settings steer only idle units on AI auto-move, so every withdrawal here is ordered.

Show the personas

core · fidelity 0

Competent commander, no nation

Fallback for unknown armies; plays the core rules only.

us · fidelity 0.6 · 1944

US rifle battalion, 1944

Methodical; strong with support weapons, slow without them.

  • Lead with fire: mortars and MGs on the objective before any rifle squad moves. company.infantry.attack company.mortar.attack
  • Put the main line on the reverse slope when the forward slope is under observed fire. c-US-3001
  • Counter infiltration with posts that hold alone and a reserve that strikes hard. company.infantry.infiltration
  • Prefer waiting for fire support over a bare assault. larp lore, fidelity 0.7+

uk · fidelity 0.6 · 1944

British infantry battalion, 1944

Careful and smoke-heavy; rarely overextends.

  • Screen every crossing of open ground; move once the smoke is thick. company.infantry.smoke
  • Consolidate at once on each objective before the next bound. squad.infantry.assault
  • Stick to the fire plan's objectives; exploit only inside them. larp lore, fidelity 0.7+

ger · fidelity 0.7 · 1944

German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine)

Aggressive counterattacks; dangerous to push into. German doctrine here is reported by other nations.

  • Counterattack a lost position at once, close behind the fire, at the flank of the break-in. c-GER-0044
  • Build strongpoints round MGs, heavy mortars and an SP gun, firing all round. c-GER-3021
  • One narrow main effort with the heavy weapons massed behind it. battalion.infantry.attack

su · fidelity 0.9 · 1941

Soviet rifle regiment, summer 1941

Larp lore, not doctrine: frontal and costly on purpose. Its own manuals asked for initiative; this persona plays the 1941 reputation.

  • Attack straight down the ordered axis; do not shift to a found gap. larp lore, fidelity 0.7+ breaks doctrine on purpose
  • Hold or counterattack; withdraw only on a direct order from the top. larp lore, fidelity 0.7+ breaks doctrine on purpose
  • Feed the reserve into a stalled attack rather than holding it back. larp lore, fidelity 0.7+ breaks doctrine on purpose

su · fidelity 0.7 · 1944

Soviet Guards rifle division, 1944

Heavy, fast main blow and bold exploitation.

  • Mass most forces and fire on the main blow where ground gives cover and observation. c-SU-2001
  • On finding a gap, leaders push through on their own, even off direction. c-SU-0018
  • Fix a town frontally with part; send the main blow round to its rear. c-SU-3019

jp · fidelity 0.8 · 1942

Japanese infantry, 1942 (reported doctrine)

Flanking and night attacks; at high fidelity it charges when losing. All doctrine here is reported by the US and UK.

  • Fake strength in front with noise and automatic fire while the main force goes round a flank. c-JP-2003
  • Under a holding attack, send LMG and grenade patrols round the flanks into the rear. c-JP-2005
  • Prefer attacks when vision is short. company.infantry.night
  • When a group is losing, charge instead of falling back. larp lore, fidelity 0.7+ breaks doctrine on purpose

fi · fidelity 0.8 · 1940

Finnish battalion, winter 1939-40

Needs a mod with a Finnish army or a winter map; maps to no stock army. Finnish practice here is reported.

  • Use snipers heavily from hides, as reported of Finnish practice. c-FI-3001 c-FI-3002
  • Ambush road-bound columns from the woods. company.infantry.ambush battalion.infantry.winter
  • Cut a stalled column into pockets and destroy them one by one. larp lore, fidelity 0.7+

core · fidelity 0

What-if: modern ideas on a WW2 force

Not period play: re-plans on events, commits the reserve behind success. For comparison against period personas.

Modern ideas: m.ooda, m.mission-command, m.recon-pull, m.find-fix-finish, m.culmination

Mission kits

Each kit is one tactic as a playable match: who attacks whom, what the map needs, how it is won, and the rules a good bot follows.

Hedgerow fields, Normandy 1944 US rifle battalion, 1944 attacks German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine)

Attacker US rifle battalion, 1944, company. Defender German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine), platoon.

Map small fields, hedges, sunken lanes. Win Attacker takes three field flags in turn before time runs out.

Teaches Tanks and infantry clear one field at a time, each covering the other.

Doctrine Tank company attack, with infantry, Company attack

  • Tanks envelop; infantry first if obstacles: Default: support fires frontally, tanks go under cover to a flank. Known AT obstacles or fortifications: infantry first, tanks fire from behind. When tanks lead, infantry follows at once, in small groups clear of the tanks.
  • Something fires while something moves: Split: base of fire pins, maneuver moves. They may swap. Site the base to fire obliquely, about 0.6 to 0.8 x mg from the objective (design). Maneuver goes by a covered route that isn't the obvious one, never a wide loop in the open.
  • Assault guns at the main effort, tank destroyers kept out of close combat: Assault guns go with the infantry of the main effort, firing HE on the points that hold it up. Tank destroyers wait in overwatch for tanks, away from close enemy infantry, with their own infantry or MG cover. Either can fire on bunkers once enemy AT is suppressed.
Hold the reverse slope German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine) attacks British infantry battalion, 1944

Attacker German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine), company. Defender British infantry battalion, 1944, platoon.

Map ridge, open forward slope. Win Defender holds the crest-line flag to the end.

Teaches Defend behind the crest and counterattack troops that come over it.

Doctrine Reverse-slope defense, Counterattack

  • Hold behind the crest when the forward slope is watched: Main position just behind the crest, out of sight of enemy units beyond close range; weapons laid on the crest line. One or two outposts on the forward slope or crest to see and warn; they fall back on contact. Most of the force held back as a counterattack group aimed at the crest.
  • Hit the flank before he organizes: Go at once, whole, at the flank of the penetration. Fire across its base to stop more entering. Stop at the old line. Beyond it, fire only.
  • Machine guns in enfilade, crossing fire, no gap at the flanks: Site MGs on the flanks of the position, firing across the front, not straight ahead. Neighbouring MGs' fields cross; check each flank is covered. Heavy MGs take the long fixed lines; light MGs fill the gaps near posts.
Forest road in winter Soviet rifle regiment, summer 1941 attacks Finnish battalion, winter 1939-40

Attacker Soviet rifle regiment, summer 1941, company. Defender Finnish battalion, winter 1939-40, platoon.

Map snow, dense forest, one road. Win The column reaches the far road flag, or the defender cuts it into two or more pieces.

Teaches A road-bound force in forest is ambushed in pieces.

Doctrine Winter fighting, Ambush

  • Ambush in close ground, open on the main body, leave fast: Two or more parties on both sides of the route, staggered so their fire does not cross into each other. Hold fire until the main body is in close range; let the scouts through. One unit opens the ambush, all fire at once; first targets are leaders, AT crews and vehicles stopped by mines.
  • In winter, shelter and roads decide: Value villages and woods more when choosing axes and held points. Expect slow off-road flanks; plan shorter maneuvers. Check tank routes before committing them.
  • Snipers hunt hidden weapons and leaders; watch roofs and tempt fire: Own sniper: forward or on a flank, apart from the platoon; first targets are MG crews, AT crews, officers and spotters. Move after firing or after a miss; mark targets for MGs and mortars. Against enemy snipers: watch roofs, towers and steeples; clear them early.
Encircle the town, 1944 Soviet Guards rifle division, 1944 attacks German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine)

Attacker Soviet Guards rifle division, 1944, battalion. Defender German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine), company.

Map town, open approaches, roads behind. Win The attacker takes the road flag behind the town and the town centre.

Teaches Fix the town frontally and send the main blow round it.

Doctrine Clearing a village, Assault guns and tank destroyers

  • Fire down the street, clear from the back, leave a way out: Bypass with leading groups if possible; a following group clears. Fire element suppresses street-facing windows; assault elements enter from the rear. Assault sections alternate clearing and covering; fire element moves up in bounds.
  • Assault guns at the main effort, tank destroyers kept out of close combat: Assault guns go with the infantry of the main effort, firing HE on the points that hold it up. Tank destroyers wait in overwatch for tanks, away from close enemy infantry, with their own infantry or MG cover. Either can fire on bunkers once enemy AT is suppressed.
  • One main effort, on the best-covered ground: Score axes by cover on the way in and by enemy strength; pick one. Team: one bot or pair is main effort, the others hold or fix. Bot: most maneuver groups on that axis; the rest press to split the enemy.
Noise in front, attack on the flank, 1942 Japanese infantry, 1942 (reported doctrine) attacks British infantry battalion, 1944

Attacker Japanese infantry, 1942 (reported doctrine), company. Defender British infantry battalion, 1944, platoon.

Map jungle or dense woods, one track. Win The attacker takes the rear flag.

Teaches Don't swing the whole defence to face the noise; keep a reserve for the flank.

Doctrine Bait and deception, Infiltration and its counter

  • Bait to find him, hold fire against his bait: A cheap element shows itself or fires; hidden killers are laid where a reply would come from and hit it at once. Only units named for it engage scouts and lone vehicles; AT guns hold to the set range. Feint on a second axis; if it finds weakness it becomes the main effort.
  • Pass small groups through unwatched ground; counter with all-round posts: Attack: send a small, well-armed group (SMG, MG, light mortar) along the unwatched route while the main attack holds the front. Its targets are the enemy's rear: heavy weapons, AT guns, crews, and the line the main attack must cross. Defense: every post can fire all round; do not pull posts back when infiltrators appear.
  • Keep a support, spend it whole, rebuild it: Exposed flank or unclear enemy: hold back more, up to two of three groups. Hold while fires or other groups can restart the attack. Commit whole, at once, at a flank or at weakness; never reinforce strong resistance.
Break a bunker line US rifle battalion, 1944 attacks German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine)

Attacker US rifle battalion, 1944, company. Defender German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine), platoon.

Map bunkers, wire, open ground. Win The attacker destroys or takes two of three bunkers.

Teaches Fire on the embrasures and smoke the bunker's neighbours while engineers close in.

Doctrine Pillbox and bunker assault, Smoke

  • Hold the embrasures, blind it, cut a lane, close from the flank: Find it: embrasures, and where it can flank the approach. Guns, tanks or MGs fire on the embrasures from a flank; smoke blinds the rest. Engineers clear wire or mines; the assault party closes from the side the embrasures don't cover, with flame or charges.
  • Smoke on the enemy, timed to the move: Located target in range: HE. Unlocated or out of range: smoke on it or its field of view. Smoke the enemy weapon, never a curtain in front of own units. Start just before the move, keep it up until cover: rounds = (gap / speed) / profile smoke life (vanilla about 60 s, the overhaul mod's grenade about 90 s).
  • Lift late, shift guns to the flanks: Close to the nearest point that doesn't mask supporting fire, then assault. Before that, move guns toward the flank of the resistance, so they fire longest. When masked, mg and mortars shift to enemy beside or behind the objective.
Force a river line Soviet Guards rifle division, 1944 attacks German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine)

Attacker Soviet Guards rifle division, 1944, company. Defender German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine), platoon.

Map river, one bridge, fords. Win The attacker holds a far-bank flag for the last third of the match.

Teaches Cross wide on a screened front and dig in on the far bank before the counterattack.

Doctrine River crossing

  • Crossings are chokes; several points, then rally: Cover the far bank with fire before anything crosses. Cross at more than one point when the map allows. Infantry first, abreast; heavy weapons and vehicles after the far bank holds.
  • Smoke on the enemy, timed to the move: Located target in range: HE. Unlocated or out of range: smoke on it or its field of view. Smoke the enemy weapon, never a curtain in front of own units. Start just before the move, keep it up until cover: rounds = (gap / speed) / profile smoke life (vanilla about 60 s, the overhaul mod's grenade about 90 s).
  • Go past the objective, then dig in: Don't stop on it: move a short way past (design 0.1 to 0.2 x rifle). Bring mg and light AT up at once to cover front and open flanks. If not advancing, set all-round defense and enter cover.
Retake the village at dawn German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine) attacks US rifle battalion, 1944

Attacker German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine), company. Defender US rifle battalion, 1944, company.

Map village, orchards. Win The defender has just taken the village. The attacker must retake it, and the defender must consolidate in time.

Teaches Consolidate quickly, and counterattack before the enemy has.

Doctrine Counterattack, Company defense

  • Hit the flank before he organizes: Go at once, whole, at the flank of the penetration. Fire across its base to stop more entering. Stop at the old line. Beyond it, fire only.
  • Go past the objective, then dig in: Don't stop on it: move a short way past (design 0.1 to 0.2 x rifle). Bring mg and light AT up at once to cover front and open flanks. If not advancing, set all-round defense and enter cover.
  • Keep a support, spend it whole, rebuild it: Exposed flank or unclear enemy: hold back more, up to two of three groups. Hold while fires or other groups can restart the attack. Commit whole, at once, at a flank or at weakness; never reinforce strong resistance.
Night attack on a perimeter Japanese infantry, 1942 (reported doctrine) attacks US rifle battalion, 1944

Attacker Japanese infantry, 1942 (reported doctrine), company. Defender US rifle battalion, 1944, platoon.

Map night or fog, perimeter, scrub. Win The attacker takes the command-post flag.

Teaches Short vision favours whoever is closest and quietest. MGs on fixed lines hold the perimeter.

Doctrine Night attack

  • Night or low vision means straight ahead and simple: Keep groups in column and deploy only close to the objective. No envelopment: one direct assault on a point already scouted. Narrow each weapon's sector and raise density on the line.
  • Machine guns in enfilade, crossing fire, no gap at the flanks: Site MGs on the flanks of the position, firing across the front, not straight ahead. Neighbouring MGs' fields cross; check each flank is covered. Heavy MGs take the long fixed lines; light MGs fill the gaps near posts.
Pursue a withdrawing enemy What-if: modern ideas on a WW2 force attacks German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine)

Attacker What-if: modern ideas on a WW2 force, company. Defender German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine), company.

Map open country, crossroads, a delay line. Win The defender gets half its force past the crossroads flag.

Teaches Push a fast group past the rearguard. The withdrawal is always ordered, not left to auto-move.

Doctrine Pursuit, Delay and withdrawal

  • Pursue at once, broad and fast, to a set limit: Go at once with the nearest fast units; don't wait for neighbours. Press on a broad front against his flanks; send groups by the shortest routes to cut his retreat. Bring MGs, mortars and guns forward so he can't re-form.
  • Leave early, covering in turn: Go before the enemy is within 0.5 x rifle or rifle fire is hurting you. One part covers while the rest moves, then swap. Last out has a covered route. Delay: spread wide, fire from maximum range, then go when he deploys.

Modding SDK

The doctrine ships as data a mod can load, plus small local tools that check, score and explain bot play. No model runs in any of them.

Data and schema

Schema version 1 holds 38 rules, 9 personas, 7 voices, 10 missions, 2 mod profiles. The export comes as doctrine.json and doctrine.lua; both carry a schema version, and a breaking change raises it. A pack under packs/<name>/ adds claims, compartments, rules, personas, voices, missions or test scenarios without touching the core; the linter checks it the same way.

ToolDoes
exportWrites the JSON and Lua doctrine, with rules, personas, voices, missions and mod profiles.
lintChecks word budgets, citations, persona traits, voice length and pack layout.
missionsWrites one briefing per mission kit.
voicePicks a chat line for a persona and event, the same line for the same seed.
aarTurns a match log into an after-action report.
evalScores answers to the scenario test set.
profile --gameReads a mod's unit and AI values into a profile.

After-action reports

A match log is one JSON object per line: time, side, group, event, and optionally the rule, the objective, whether the move was ordered or engine auto-move, and whether the front was succeeding. The report ties each event to a rule and marks it followed, departed, or in character for the persona. Both samples below are hand-written logs; the game does not write this log yet.

After-action report: sample-larp-1941.jsonl

Generated by tools/aar.mjs from the log, no model. 7 events over 6:40; side A: loss.

SidePersonaFidelityFollowedDepartedIn character
Asu-1941-rifle0.9111
Bger-1944-kampfgruppe0.7010

Timeline

  • 0:50 A 1st Bn: departed tac.fire-and-move. Assault with no fire or smoke in the 60 s before it.
  • 2:00 A 2nd Bn: in character tac.reserve. Reserve fed into a failing front at Hill 204. Doctrine commits it behind success. In character for su-1941-rifle (larp lore): "Feed the reserve into a stalled attack rather than holding it back."
  • 3:20 A 1st Bn: followed tac.withdrawal. Ordered withdrawal.
  • 3:50 B Kampfgruppe: departed tac.counterattack. No counterattack within 60 s of losing Village.

Lessons

  • tac.fire-and-move: Split: base of fire pins, maneuver moves. They may swap.
  • tac.counterattack: Go at once, whole, at the flank of the penetration.

A departure marked "in character" is what that persona is meant to do at its fidelity, so it does not count against it.

After-action report: sample-log.jsonl

Generated by tools/aar.mjs from the log, no model. 16 events over 8:00; side A: loss.

SidePersonaFidelityFollowedDepartedIn character
Aus-1944-rifle0.6230
Bger-1944-kampfgruppe0.7210

Timeline

  • 1:00 A 1st Plt: followed tac.fire-and-move. Assault went in behind fire or smoke.
  • 1:35 A 1st Plt: followed tac.consolidate. Consolidated on Field 1 in time.
  • 2:50 B 2. Zug: followed tac.counterattack. Counterattacked Field 1 within a minute.
  • 3:50 A 2nd Plt: departed tac.fire-and-move. Assault with no fire or smoke in the 60 s before it.
  • 4:20 A 2nd Plt: departed tac.withdrawal. Fell back on engine auto-move, not by order. Retreat settings only steer idle units on auto-move; doctrine wants an ordered withdrawal by bounds with a rear cover.
  • 5:00 A Reserve: departed tac.reserve. Reserve fed into a failing front at Field 2. Doctrine commits it behind success.
  • 6:00 B 1. Zug: departed tac.consolidate. No consolidation within 90 s of taking Field 2.
  • 7:00 B Reserve: followed tac.reserve. Reserve committed behind success at Field 2.

Lessons

  • tac.fire-and-move: Split: base of fire pins, maneuver moves. They may swap.
  • tac.withdrawal: Go before the enemy is within 0.5 x rifle or rifle fire is hurting you.
  • tac.reserve: Exposed flank or unclear enemy: hold back more, up to two of three groups.
  • tac.consolidate: Don't stop on it: move a short way past (design 0.1 to 0.2 x rifle).

A departure marked "in character" is what that persona is meant to do at its fidelity, so it does not count against it.

Show the 30 scenarios

Modern layer (optional)

Post-war ideas that sharpen the WW2 compartments. They are not WW2 doctrine, no rule cites them, and removing them changes nothing above.

Show the modern layer

modern / Boyd, Patterns of Conflict briefing (1986)

Decision cycle (OODA)

observeorientdecideacttempo

Whoever completes observe-orient-decide-act faster forces the other side to react to stale pictures. Speed of re-planning matters more than speed of units.

In game Re-plan on events (contact, loss, flag change), not on a fixed timer. Two simultaneous threats cost the opposing bot more than one strong one.

Caution A faster loop with bad orientation just makes mistakes quicker; keep the scouting step.

Sharpens: company.infantry.deception, company.infantry.infiltration, company.infantry.pursuit

modern / ADP 6-0 Mission Command (US Army)

Mission command

intenttaskfreedominitiative

Give each group the purpose and the end state, not a route. Lower levels pick the method and act on chances without asking.

In game Team or bot level issues an objective plus purpose (seize, fix, screen); the group layer chooses its path and may exploit a gap inside that purpose.

Caution Needs a shared rule for when a group may abandon its task; otherwise groups drift.

Sharpens: company.infantry.attack, battalion.infantry.attack

modern / MCDP 1 Warfighting (USMC)

Maneuver warfare

surfacesgapsshockdislocation

Avoid enemy strength and push through weakness to strike what holds the enemy together, rather than wearing down every position.

In game Score sectors by enemy density; route the main effort at low-density sectors toward flags or guns behind the line.

Caution Small AS2 maps often have no real gap; fall back to fix-and-flank.

Sharpens: company.infantry.infiltration, battalion.tank.attack, company.infantry.pursuit

modern / Lind, Maneuver Warfare Handbook (1985); MCDP 1

Recon-pull and surfaces and gaps

scout leadsfollow successreinforce gaps

Scouts find where the enemy is thin; the main body is pulled to that gap instead of pushed along a fixed axis.

In game Keep the reserve uncommitted until scout reports or early progress pick an axis; send it after success, not to rescue a stalled attack.

Caution Needs live scouting; without it this is a guess.

Sharpens: platoon.recon.recon, company.infantry.approach, battalion.infantry.attack

modern / FM 3-21.8 Infantry Rifle Platoon and Squad; ATP 3-21.8

Movement techniques

travelingoverwatchboundingcontact likely

Pick the movement method by how likely contact is: travel fast when unlikely, have one element watch while another moves when possible, and bound alternately when expected.

In game Three movement modes keyed to distance from last known enemy (in profile vision ratios): column move, one-up-one-watching, alternate bounds.

Caution Bounding is slow; on tight timers use it only inside likely-contact range.

Sharpens: squad.infantry.attack, platoon.infantry.attack, company.tank.attack

modern / FM 3-90 Tactics; British Army Field Manual tactics doctrine

Suppression as an effect

neutralizesuppresswindowshift fire

Fire is judged by what it stops the enemy doing, for how long. The assault must move inside the suppression window and fire shifts as it closes.

In game Tie the assault group's go signal to support fire actually landing; if the game has no suppression model, use smoke and fire volume as the proxy.

Caution Stock AS2 morale follows health, so the effect is weaker than doctrine assumes.

Sharpens: company.mg.attack, company.mortar.attack, squad.infantry.assault, company.infantry.smoke

modern / ADP 3-0 Operations (US Army)

Defeat mechanisms

destroydislocatedisintegrateisolate

Name how the enemy will be beaten: destroy forces, dislocate them so their position is useless, disintegrate their control, or isolate them from support.

In game Plan label for a bot: destroy (trade), dislocate (flank past), isolate (cut a sector off and take its flags).

Caution Labels only help if they change buys and routes.

Sharpens: battalion.infantry.attack, company.infantry.ambush, battalion.at.defense

modern / FM 3-90 Tactics; Clausewitz, On War (culminating point)

Tempo and culmination

momentumculminating pointtransitionconsolidate

Every attack weakens as it goes. Stop and consolidate before strength falls below what the defender can counter, or keep going only while momentum lasts.

In game Track own strength against the start of the push; under a threshold, switch the group to consolidate and dig in on the gained flag.

Caution Threshold is a design value, not a source value.

Sharpens: squad.infantry.assault, company.infantry.counterattack, company.infantry.pursuit

modern / FM 3-90 Tactics; common NATO teaching

Find, fix, finish

findfixfinishexploit

Locate the enemy with the least force, pin it in place with fire, then destroy it with the main effort, and exploit if it breaks.

In game Group state machine: scout until contact, support group fixes, assault group finishes, reserve exploits.

Caution Fixing needs a real base of fire; with too few MGs, use mortar or tank fire.

Sharpens: company.infantry.attack, platoon.infantry.attack, company.assault-gun.attack

modern / MCDP 1 Warfighting; ADP 3-90 Offense and Defense

Combined arms dilemma

dilemmamutual supportno good answer

Use arms together so any defense against one exposes the enemy to another: hiding from guns invites infantry, fighting infantry exposes to tanks.

In game Attack groups pair tanks with infantry and indirect fire; count it as a pitfall when a group attacks with one arm only.

Caution Coordination is the hard part; a pairing that moves at different speeds breaks apart.

Sharpens: battalion.tank.attack, squad.infantry.tank-hunting, battalion.at.defense, company.tank.attack

How solid this is

Claims came from two reading passes of different depth. A number from the lighter pass is never used as a game parameter until it is checked against its page.

  • Coverage. 34 of 3,184 selected pages stayed unread after two passes: 31 Soviet and 3 Japanese. Pages were selected by script, so a page the script dropped was never read.
  • Nations. Germany is mostly reported by others. Japan and Italy are reported only. UK company attack rests on a 1937 manual. Soviet text has mediocre OCR (text read by machine from page scans).
  • Numbers. Checked against OCR text, not against page images, so a misread digit could remain.
  • Untitled sources. A few sources have no title in the pack, so their citations name them as an untitled source with a fixed number.
  • Thin compartments. Sniper, winter and engineer are thin and rest mostly on the lighter pass. There is no cavalry compartment: the only rows were Polish training-control text, and it has little use in the game.
  • Rule values. A distance marked design is a starting value. None have been tuned, because nothing has been played.
